title: Ask Evelo: Should we wait for mortgage rates to drop before buying?
hook: "Should we just wait until rates come down?" It's one of the first questions buyers in Fishers and Westfield ask us.
body:
It's a fair question, and there isn't one right answer for everyone. Waiting can work. It can also cost you in ways that are easy to miss.

Right now, buyers have room to choose. Hamilton County had 1,111 homes for sale in October, up 19.3% from a year earlier. That means more homes to compare and more time to decide in Fishers, Westfield and Noblesville. If rates fall, that choice could shrink as other buyers jump back in at the same moment.

So instead of guessing what rates will do, start with what you can control: the monthly payment you're comfortable with, the cash you have for a down payment and closing costs, and how long you plan to stay. If those numbers work today, buying now can make sense. If they don't, waiting is a perfectly good plan.

Source: Realtor.com via FRED, Oct 2026.

title: Ask Evelo: What is my Fishers home worth? 4 factors beyond the online estimate
hook: Two online estimates, two different numbers. So what is your Fishers home actually worth?
body:
Probably neither number, exactly. An algorithm can't walk through your kitchen. These 4 factors matter more:

1. Recent comparable sales. Homes like yours that closed nearby, adjusted for real differences.
2. Current competition. Hamilton County had 1,111 homes for sale in October, and buyers compare.
3. Condition and updates. A newer roof or a remodeled kitchen can separate two homes on the same street.
4. Location details. Lot, floor plan and which part of Fishers, from 46037 to 46038.

A Comparative Market Analysis (CMA) pulls these together into a price range built on your home, not a formula.

Source: Realtor.com via FRED, Oct 2026.

title: Market Pulse: 55 median days on market in the metro, what sellers should plan for
hook: 55 days. That's how long the typical home for sale in the Indianapolis metro sat on the market in October.
body:
Closer to home, Hamilton County homes moved a little faster, at 49 days. Either way, that's slower than the spring rush, and it's worth planning around if you want to sell this winter or early spring.

What that looks like in practice:
• Build in time. Plan your move, and any purchase, around a longer stretch between listing and contract.
• Price it right from the start. Buyers have homes to compare, and they notice when a price doesn't match the condition.
• Prep matters more. Small repairs, clean photos and a clear list of updates help a home in Fishers or Noblesville stand out.

A slower pace isn't a bad market. It's a market that rewards planning.

Source: Realtor.com via FRED, Oct 2026.

title: Market Pulse: 55.4% of metro listings had a price cut, how buyers can use it fairly
hook: More than half of the homes for sale around Indianapolis took a price cut in October. Here's how to use that without insulting a seller.
body:
Across the metro, 55.4% of active listings had a price reduction. For buyers looking in Fishers, Carmel or Noblesville, that can mean a little more room to negotiate. It doesn't mean every seller will take any offer.

Leverage isn't the same as lowballing. A very low offer on a well-priced home can end the conversation before it starts. A better approach:
• Check the history. How long has the home been listed, and has the price already moved?
• Let recent sales in that neighborhood set your number, not the discount you hope for.
• Ask for more than price. Help with closing costs, or repairs after inspection, can matter as much as a lower number.

A fair, well-supported offer gives a seller a reason to say yes.

Source: Realtor.com via FRED, Oct 2026.

title: Market Pulse: rates in context at 7.28%, a payment-first way to plan
hook: Start with the payment, not the rate.
body:
The average 30-year fixed rate was 7.28% for the week of Nov 19. Headlines will keep tracking that number. Your budget runs on a monthly payment.

Here's a local way to use it. Say you're looking at homes near Hamilton County's October median list price of $445,000. Before you tour a single one, ask a lender to show you the full monthly payment at today's rate, including Hamilton County property taxes, insurance and any HOA dues. Taxes and dues vary between Fishers, Carmel and Noblesville neighborhoods, so the same price can carry different payments.

Then flip it around:
1. Pick the monthly number that feels comfortable.
2. Ask the lender to turn it into a price range.
3. Search inside that range, not at the very top of it.

This keeps the decision about your life, not about a weekly average you can't control.

Source: Freddie Mac via FRED, week of Nov 19, 2026; Realtor.com via FRED, Oct 2026.

title: Ask Evelo: Three January tasks that make a spring 2027 move calmer
hook: Three January tasks that make a spring move calmer.
body:
In Hamilton County, the typical home for sale sat on the market for 49 days in October. Add time to prepare and to close, and a spring move really starts in winter. Here is a simple January checklist:

1. Get pre-approved. Talk with a lender about your budget, down payment and monthly comfort zone. It turns a rough guess into a real range.
2. Have a pricing conversation. If you're selling, learn what your home could list for based on recent sales and current competition. Your home will have its own number.
3. Set a timeline. Work backward from your ideal move date to plan prep, listing, showings and closing.

None of this commits you to anything. It just means you'll be ready when the right home, or the right offer, comes along.

Source: Realtor.com via FRED, Oct 2026.
